target_customer: Engineering and platform teams at companies using multiple LLM providers; enterprise gateway customers
problem: Each LLM provider has its own API, so teams struggle to switch models, track spend and enforce access; LiteLLM exposes 100+ models through the OpenAI format.
business_model: Open-source SDK and proxy with paid enterprise gateway features (pricing not found)

founders.name: Krrish Dholakia
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; no background given there.

founders.name: Ishaan Jaffer
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page and described in the launch post as a maintainer.

technical_complexity.rationale: Translating many provider APIs into one format is mostly engineering effort, but keeping up with fast-changing providers and running a reliable proxy at scale is demanding.

defensibility.rationale: Open source and MIT licensed, so copyable; adoption and integrations built a large community that acts as a soft moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Cloud AI gateways and managed routers emerged; LiteLLM stayed the leading open-source option with over 50K GitHub stars per the YC page.

market_need_then: After ChatGPT's launch in late 2022, developers needed to call several competing LLM APIs with different formats, and the OpenAI format became a de facto standard.

identity.mascot_or_character: Train emoji used in the GitHub README header (reason not stated)

branding.brand_signature: The train emoji in the GitHub README title
branding.community_and_virality: Over 50K GitHub stars and 1,700+ contributors per company pages (self-reported); widely covered by security press after 2026 incidents.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong developer recognition through open-source adoption and wide mention in alternatives roundups, but little distinctive visual identity.

outcome_analysis: LiteLLM grew from a YC W23 open-source library into a widely used gateway with large enterprise logos and a team of about 20. Adoption came from open-source distribution and the need for provider-neutral APIs. In 2026 it suffered two reported supply chain incidents (March and October) and litigation was reported in April 2026, which are risks to trust for a package that holds provider API keys.
notes: The $1.6M seed from YC, Gravity Fund and Pioneer Fund comes from the company's YC page; its date is not stated and secondary sources conflict (2023 versus 2026), so the round date is null. CB Insights shows only about $500K over 3 rounds and other trackers list other totals; a $16M figure on an aggregator was not supported by any primary source and is ignored. No competitor source dated near the 2023 batch was found (searches returned 2026 alternative roundups), so the list is empty. Security incidents: March 2026 (versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8) per company post-mortem; a second incident reported October 2026 per Help Net Security.
